sources.title: HypRQ-VAE: Hyperbolic Item Indexing for Long-Tail-Aware Generative Recommender Systems
sources.full_text_basis: arXiv provides a linked PDF; title and abstract metadata retrieved from arXiv API. PDF availability is independently checkable at the linked source; this audit did not inspect the full PDF contents.

overlap.user_next_item_behavior: ABSTRACT — frames sequential recommendation as item-ID sequences and evaluates a generative recommender; does not establish that the method specifically models a user's next-item transition beyond that framing.
overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: ABSTRACT — explicitly proposes hyperbolic residual-quantized VAE for item indexing and motivates it via hierarchy and long-tail structure.
overlap.generative_semantic_ids: ABSTRACT — item indexing/vocabulary for generative recommender; semantically informed item representations are described, but the abstract does not explicitly call the codes Semantic IDs (SIDs).
overlap.all_three: PARTIAL; not verified as an exact three-way intersection.

limitations: No independently verified source was found in this search with explicit evidence for all three elements together: user-level next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry, and generative semantic IDs.

FULL_TEXT labels indicate a publicly linked arXiv PDF exists, not that full-text contents were read. Specific overlap statements are conservatively labeled ABSTRACT because the evidence retrieved was the arXiv API abstract.
UNKNOWN means absent from retrieved evidence, not proof that a feature is absent from the paper.

HypRQ-VAE is the closest apparent intersection, but the abstract's phrasing is generative recommendation and hyperbolic item indexing; user-specific next-item prediction and explicit semantic-ID generation need full-text verification.
The findings are search-bounded and should not be interpreted as proof that no exact-intersection paper exists. No prior-candidate prompts or unseen future/test interactions were used.
